findings.explanation: HOL4 defines FAPPLY f x = OUTL (fmap_REP f x). sumTheory specifies OUTL only by OUTL (INL x) = x (sumScript.sml:286), so OUTL (INR ()) is open. Off the domain, HOL4 saves only NOT_FDOM_FAPPLY_FEMPTY (FAPPLY f x = FAPPLY FEMPTY x); FAPPLY_DEF also gives one fixed value per range type. Neither determines that value. Lean fills the none case with ARB, so FAPPLY FEMPTY x = ARB holds by rfl, as does FAPPLY f x = ARB for every x not in FDOM f. It also proves FAPPLY FEMPTY x = HD []. HOL4 leaves all these equations open, for example at range type bool.
findings.repair:
def Aux.OUTL_spec {β : Type v} (o : Option β → β) : Prop := ∀ y, o (some y) = y

def Aux.OUTL {β : Type v} [Nonempty β] : Option β → β := Classical.epsilon (Aux.OUTL_spec (β := β))

theorem Aux.OUTL_def {β : Type v} [Nonempty β] : Aux.OUTL_spec (Aux.OUTL (β := β)) := by
  apply Classical.epsilon_spec (p := Aux.OUTL_spec (β := β))
  exact ⟨fun o => match o with | some y => y | none => Classical.choice inferInstance, fun _ => rfl⟩

def FAPPLY {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [Nonempty β] (f : fmap α β) (x : α) : β := Aux.OUTL (f.rep x)

-- and end the proof of FUN_FMAP_DEF with: simp [FAPPLY, hx', Aux.OUTL_def (f x)]
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.Prelude.FiniteMap

open HOL

theorem chk1 {α : Type} {β : Type} [Nonempty β] (x : α) :
    HOL.FAPPLY (HOL.FEMPTY : HOL.fmap α β) x = (HOL.ARB : β) := rfl

theorem chk2 {α : Type} {β : Type} [Nonempty β] (x : α) :
    HOL.FAPPLY (HOL.FEMPTY : HOL.fmap α β) x = HOL.HD ([] : List β) := rfl
findings.hol4_check: ?outl:bool + one -> bool. (!x. outl (INL x) = x) /\ outl (INR ()) <> ARB
